title: Recover from a frozen bank account or bank failure
summary: Whether it's a compliance freeze or your bank failing outright, the clock is payroll — and that is true in every country. The first hours are confirming what happened, sizing exposure against your deposit-protection scheme's limit (US: FDIC insurance at $250,000 per depositor, per bank, per ownership category; the UK/German/French/Indian schemes and their caps ride in the geo notes), and getting a second operating account live so the payments that cannot bounce don't. Then the honest fork: a compliance freeze is a KYC/UBO documents conversation with the bank; a failure is a receivership you track and claim against for uninsured balances (US: the FDIC's). Re-pointing banking rails mid-crisis is undoable only at real cost — that's the painful part, stated.

parts.title: Confirm what happened: a compliance freeze notice from the bank, or the bank itself failing (US: the FDIC failed-bank list; your country's resolution authority otherwise)
Size the exposure: balances against your deposit-protection limit (US: FDIC's $250,000 per depositor, per bank, per ownership category — other schemes in the geo notes)
Triage the next payroll run and the payments that cannot bounce
Open a backup operating account at a second bank
Re-point the rails: processor payouts in, payroll and vendor payments out
If it's a compliance freeze: ask what triggered the review and supply the KYC/UBO documents the bank asks for
If the bank failed: track the receivership (US: the FDIC's) and file the claim for uninsured balances
Wait for the freeze review or the receivership distributions

metadata.trigger: Your operating account is frozen by the bank's compliance review — or the bank itself fails.
metadata.supportReason: Opening the backup account is KYC-gated, the freeze conversation is with the bank's compliance team, and the FDIC claim is theirs to process. An agent can size the insurance exposure from your balances; it cannot unfreeze an account.

contextNeeded.query: which bank, which accounts, and current balances
the next payroll date and critical payment schedule

geoNotes.summary: If a UK-authorised bank fails, the FSCS protects £85,000 per depositor per bank and aims to pay most depositors within days; a compliance freeze is the same KYC/UBO documents conversation with the bank — and standing up a second operating account for payroll is the same first move.

The statutory Entschädigungseinrichtung deutscher Banken (EdB) compensates €100,000 per depositor per bank (the EU deposit-guarantee floor) and contacts depositors after a failure; compliance freezes are worked out with the bank's own team under BaFin supervision.

The FGDR guarantees €100,000 per depositor per bank and targets compensation within seven working days of a failure; a gel du compte lifts on the bank's KYC questions being answered, not on a form — the backup-account move is identical.

DICGC insurance covers ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank (principal plus interest), and RBI moratoria on stressed banks have historically capped withdrawals for months — which makes the second-account triage even more important than in the US.
